bib.title: SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills

question: How should an agent skill document be optimized so that a frozen agent improves reliably under feedback, with the controls of weight-space training?
hypothesis: Treating the skill as the trainable external state, with bounded edits, a held-out acceptance gate, a rejected-edit buffer and an epoch-wise slow/meta update, gives stable gains over one-shot, human-written and other optimized skills.
contributions: Formulate agent-skill learning as optimization over an external natural-language state and introduce SkillOpt, a harness-agnostic optimizer with rollout batches, reflection minibatches, add/delete/replace edits, textual learning rates, schedules, held-out acceptance, rejected-edit buffers and epoch-wise slow/meta update.
Broad empirical study across six benchmarks, seven target models and three execution harnesses; best or tied-best on 52 of 52 cells.
Component ablations and three forms of transfer (cross-model, cross-harness, cross-benchmark).

method.summary: A frozen target model runs rollout batches with the current skill; a separate optimizer model reflects on failure and success minibatches, proposes append/insert/replace/delete edits, merges and ranks them, and clips to an edit budget Lt (textual learning rate). A candidate skill is accepted only if it strictly beats the current score on a selection split; rejected edits go to an epoch-local buffer; an epoch-end slow update writes a protected guidance block and an optimizer-side meta skill is kept. The best accepted skill is exported as best_skill.md.
method.task: Prompt/skill optimization for frozen LLM agents (QA, spreadsheets, documents, math, embodied tasks)

datasets.name: SearchQA
datasets.split: deterministic train/selection/test, split_seed=42; default 2:1:7 when none stated; ablation panel (a) uses 4:1:5

datasets.name: SpreadsheetBench
datasets.split: as above; multi-round codegen up to 30 turns, openpyxl/pandas runtime, mode=multi

datasets.name: OfficeQA
datasets.split: as above; multi-turn tool loops up to 24 tool calls

datasets.name: OlympiadBench -> Omni-MATH
datasets.source: He et al. 2024; Gao et al. 2024

other.default: inferred: GPT-5.5 (Table 5 'strong optimizer (GPT-5.5)'; ablations use GPT-5.5 as both target and optimizer)

inference.samples: Single reported score per cell on one split (split_seed=42); no repeats, seeds or error bars stated
inference.prompting: Skill prepended to the system/developer prompt in direct chat; rendered to per-task SKILL.md in Codex and Claude Code harnesses. Direct chat is a single chat completion call.

parameters.edit_budget_Lt: 4 with cosine decay, floor 2 (schedules: constant, linear, cosine, autonomous)
parameters.gate: strictly greater than current selection score; ties rejected
parameters.slow_update: 20 sampled tasks per epoch, previous vs current epoch skill; applied from epoch 2

metrics.name: Native hard score / exact-match accuracy
metrics.definition: Per-benchmark native evaluator on held-out test split

eval.protocol: Train/selection/test split; selection split only gates edits; test only for final report. All baselines use the same target model, test split and scorer. Entries not measured under the aligned protocol are marked as dashes.

prompts.text: You are an expert failure-analysis agent for AI agent tasks. You will be given MULTIPLE failed agent trajectories from a single minibatch and the current skill document. Your job is to identify the most important COMMON failure patterns across the batch and propose a concise set of skill edits.
prompts.where: Appendix C.2.1 (opening; full text and JSON schema in the PDF)

prompts.purpose: Success analysis, failure/success/final merge, ranking, slow update and meta skill prompts
prompts.text: Seven further prompt contracts (analyst_success.md, merge_failure.md, merge_success.md, merge_final.md, ranking.md, slow_update.md, meta_skill.md) are printed in full in Appendix C.2.2-C.2.8, all requiring JSON output and protecting the SLOW_UPDATE_START/END region.

limits: Needs scored trajectories and a held-out selection split; most applicable with automatic verifiers or exact-match metrics (Appendix B).
Training needs extra rollouts and optimizer calls; cost is amortized only when the skill is reused.
One skill for one domain; may not suit heterogeneous domains.
Skills can encode training-distribution heuristics; held-out check needed before transfer.
Not stated: seeds, repeats, error bars, decoding settings, dataset sizes (except ALFWorld and LiveMath), model parameter counts for GPT models.
No ablation without the validation gate, so the gate's share of the gain is not isolated.
Headline GPT-5.5 cells (87.3, 80.7 with constant schedule; 66.9 at lr=8) match sweep values, not the default row (87.1, 77.5, 61.3); selection of the headline configuration is not explained.
Baselines are run by the authors; EvoSkill is measured only on harness rows and TextGrad/GEPA only in direct chat.
Appendix C names SealQA among the benchmarks, but it appears in no table.
